answer: A sybil swarm thins when each identity must register a real basalt-soil vineyard terrace: its vine rows pruned, photographed and logged each season under a licensed agronomist's signed inspection, with a raven roost count proving the plot is a living site, not a paper farm. Faking one identity costs leasing a basalt terrace, tending vines all year, and paying an agronomist — a whole working vineyard per fake agent.
